title: What the Go SDK's ZTW packages leave out: commented-out functions, uncovered endpoints and activation
aliases: ztw go sdk workload groups create
ztw go sdk activate after change

prose.text: Which functions each ZTW package exports, and which endpoints they call, is generated (`node scripts/kb.mjs surface ztw`). This subject records the vendor code that sits in block comments and does not compile, and what the packages do not cover.

prose.label: Functions that do not compile.
prose.text: {{workload-groups-writes-commented}} {{log-rule-count-commented}} {{activation-cli-commented}} A working activation CLI ships with the Terraform provider instead: [[cloud-connector.terraform.activation]].

prose.label: Activation.
prose.text: {{no-auto-activation}} The activate and forced-activate calls are described in [[shared.activation.cbc]].

prose.label: Forwarding rules.
prose.text: {{go-no-dest-workload-groups}} The Python SDK sends that field: [[cloud-connector.sdk-python.coverage]].

prose.label: Partner integrations.
prose.text: Whether REST paths exist for Azure and GCP partner integration, which neither SDK covers, is open in [[cloud-connector.api.partner-integrations-wire]].

Two packages that write the same DNS gateway endpoint are compared in [[cloud-connector.terraform.gateways]]; the read-only ZPA-resources package is in [[cloud-connector.terraform.forwarding-rules]]; service functions that misroute or mis-assert are in [[cloud-connector.sdk-go.service-defects]].

checks.do: Whether a ZTW function is inside a block comment in the vendor source before relying on it (workload group writes, the log-rule count, the activation CLI).
Whether the Go program calls activation after its writes; nothing in the ZTW services activates for it.

workload-groups-writes-commented.statement: In the Go SDK's ZTW `workload_groups` package, `Create`, `Update` and `Delete` sit inside one block comment (it opens before `Create` and closes after `Delete`) and are not compiled; `Get`, `GetByName` and `GetAll` are outside it.

activation-cli-commented.statement: The SDK's `activation_cli/zconActivator.go` declares `package main`, but everything after that line, its imports and `main` included, is one block comment, so it is neither a runnable command nor an importable package.

no-auto-activation.statement: The Go SDK's ZTW create, update and delete functions do not activate; staged changes take effect only when the caller calls `activation.UpdateActivationStatus` or `activation.ForceActivationStatus`.
no-auto-activation.conditions: Absence: the ZTW service packages were searched at the pin for calls into the activation package or the activate endpoints; only the activation package itself uses them.

ecgroup-endpoints.statement: The Go `ecgroup` package defines only two endpoints, the group collection and its lite view, and six functions: `Get`, `GetByName`, `GetAll`, `GetEcGroupLiteID` and `GetEcGroupLiteByName` read groups and `Delete` deletes one; none creates or updates a group.

ecgroup-endpoints.conditions: The six function signatures quoted are every func declaration in ecgroup.go at the pin.

bulk-vm-ops-not-in-go.statement: So the bulk VM status, release-channel and upgrade-metrics operations of the group API have no Go SDK function; a Go program reaches them only with raw requests.
bulk-vm-ops-not-in-go.conditions: Absence: no ZTW Go package at the pin defines the releaseChannel, vmStatus or vmUpgradeMetrics paths of the group API reference (searched zscaler/ztw/services).

go-no-dest-workload-groups.statement: The Go SDK's ZTW forwarding rule struct carries source workload groups (`srcWorkloadGroups`) and no destination workload groups field.
go-no-dest-workload-groups.conditions: Absence: forwarding_rules.go was searched at the pin for workload; SrcWorkloadGroups is the only match.
